# Tabs

**Status:** Stable  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use Tabs to let experienced users switch between closely related sections of content without leaving the page.

## When to use

- Use for users who are familiar with tabbed interfaces, such as caseworkers switching between related data views.
- Use only when users do not need to compare the sections at the same time.

## When not to use

- Do not use for primary page or site navigation, or to hide steps in a journey.
- Do not use when users need to read sections in order or compare information across them.

## Anatomy

- **Tabs module (required):** The root contains a fallback contents heading, link list and corresponding panels.
- **Tab links (required):** Each ordinary anchor targets the id of one content panel.
- **Panels (required):** Each uniquely identified panel contains a heading and its complete content.

## Variants

| Variant | Element | Classes | Use |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Default | `div` | `govuk-tabs` | Two or more closely related content views for experienced users. |

## Behaviour and progressive enhancement

- Initialise govuk-tabs so wide screens receive tab semantics, keyboard behaviour and history-fragment updates.
- On narrow screens and without JavaScript, links and panels behave as an in-page table of contents rather than an inaccessible tab widget.
- Do not manually add ARIA tab roles; allow the official GOV.UK module to enhance the base markup.

## Accessibility contract

- Every tab href must match one unique panel id and every panel needs a descriptive heading.
- Keep all content in the document so it remains reachable before enhancement.
- Test keyboard navigation, back and forward navigation, and layouts at high zoom.

## Content rules

- Use short, distinct tab labels that describe the panel content.
- Keep the number of tabs small enough to remain understandable and usable on narrow screens.
- Do not repeat the same information in multiple panels.

## Token references

- `govuk.color.link`
- `govuk.color.focus`
- `govuk.color.border`
- `govuk.color.body-background`

## HTML examples

### Two related views

```html
<div class="govuk-tabs" data-module="govuk-tabs">
  <h2 class="govuk-tabs__title">Contents</h2>
  <ul class="govuk-tabs__list">
    <li class="govuk-tabs__list-item govuk-tabs__list-item--selected"><a class="govuk-tabs__tab" href="#today">Today</a></li>
    <li class="govuk-tabs__list-item"><a class="govuk-tabs__tab" href="#this-week">This week</a></li>
  </ul>
  <div class="govuk-tabs__panel" id="today"><h2 class="govuk-heading-l">Today</h2><p class="govuk-body">Today’s information.</p></div>
  <div class="govuk-tabs__panel govuk-tabs__panel--hidden" id="this-week"><h2 class="govuk-heading-l">This week</h2><p class="govuk-body">This week’s information.</p></div>
</div>
```
